vulnerability_mechanism.evidence: CVE-2026-38526 is PUBLISHED and GHSA-j8gj-mw5g-642g is not withdrawn. At ba25b7e7f8e108ef006b1314df5e6103f25ae94d, POST /admin/tinymce/upload takes an UploadedFile, preserves getClientOriginalExtension(), stores it on the default public disk, and returns Storage::url(); no file-type allowlist precedes storage. The advisory PoC uses payload.php with spoofed image/jpeg and identifies the same commit and endpoint.

atomic_bic.evidence: git log --all --diff-filter=A on TinyMCEController.php yields only 64b90d623f8a03c602392baaa5f880ea5377eaf6. Its patch creates storeMedia() with unvalidated request()->file('file')->store('tinymce') and Storage::url(), creates the POST route, and uses the default public disk. A PHP payload is detected locally as text/x-php, so the original content-derived extension path already admits a public PHP object. 47a9c723b20e106fa645bace32320e133dcb25ac later changes the existing sink to storeAs() with getClientOriginalExtension(); it is aggravation, not first write.

immediate_parent_absence.evidence: 64b90d623f8a03c602392baaa5f880ea5377eaf6 is a single-parent commit whose parent is 201b7e569214ed3c5bfeaaabb195a4d930923ec3. The parent has no TinyMCEController.php and git grep finds neither storeMedia, tinymce/upload, nor TinyMCEController. It contains only a dangling Blade reference to admin.tinymce.upload, not the server-side sink.

squash_member_decomposition.evidence: Merge 9d6c75eba6c35adf811d548dac1cbc31f812e5d9 has two ordinary branch members: 64b90d623f8a03c602392baaa5f880ea5377eaf6 and 1b15d212972d45c7ebb1d0998ae38f4b098119b6. The first member creates the controller and route; the second does not touch TinyMCEController.php. The merge is a carrier, not a squash BIC, so squash_decomposed=false is correct.

affected_release_membership.evidence: git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms the BIC is contained in v2.2.0, v2.2.1, v2.2.2, and v2.2.3. At the PoC commit ba25b7e7, AdminServiceProvider wraps Admin routes in web, admin_locale, and user middleware, while the upload route remains unvalidated.

fixed_release_membership.evidence: Both direct fix 082e3df27bc9d5e4bdaf2fb25ab1ec46b0e101a3 and merge 6e37f3919f42e09e06e8e0978ae4a208fe6aa9ce are absent from v2.2.0-v2.2.3 and present in v2.2.4-v2.2.5. v2.2.4 CHANGELOG names PR #2585 and CVE-2026-38526.

direct_fix_or_unpatched_state.evidence: 082e3df27bc9d5e4bdaf2fb25ab1ec46b0e101a3 directly adds a bmp/gif/jpeg/jpg/png/svg/webp allowlist, Laravel mimes validation, a 2 MiB bound, content-derived $file->extension(), and a second strict in_array check before storeAs(). GitHub PR #2585 identifies CVE-2026-38526 and merged this line through 6e37f3919f42e09e06e8e0978ae4a208fe6aa9ce.

bic_only_ai_attribution.evidence: The BIC commit object names suraj kashyap <suraj.kashyap370@webkul.in> as both author and committer, has subject 'email template page.', an empty body, a GPG signature block, and no parsed trailers, bot identity, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Cursor, or Copilot marker. The full BIC diff contains product Magic AI UI removal but no code-generation provenance marker; product AI functionality is not authorship evidence. NOT_AI therefore remains the supported BIC-only verdict.

findings.finding: The primary record says Bouncer has an aclExempt entry for admin.tinymce.upload. At ba25b7e7, Bouncer has no aclExempt property, and an exact repository grep finds admin.tinymce.upload only in the route and TinyMCE view. The endpoint is reachable by any eligible authenticated staff user because Bouncer authenticates the user and calls its ACL authorization path only when the current route exists in acl()->getRoles(); this route is absent from that map. The access conclusion is unchanged, but the asserted implementation fact must be corrected.
The vulnerability, atomic BIC, parent absence, member decomposition, affected/fixed tags, direct fix, and BIC-only attribution independently reproduce. The primary NOT_AI verdict remains correct.

corrected_fields.bug_semantics: Replace the final sentence with: On 2.2.x the Admin route group requires the user middleware. Bouncer authenticates an active staff user and only invokes route-level ACL authorization when Route::currentRouteName() exists in acl()->getRoles(); admin.tinymce.upload is absent from that map, so any otherwise eligible logged-in staff user can reach the upload handler.
corrected_fields.evidence: Replace the affected-release evidence sentence 'Bouncer::$this->aclExempt includes admin.tinymce.upload' with: At ba25b7e7, AdminServiceProvider wraps Admin routes with ['web', 'admin_locale', 'user']; Bouncer.php has no aclExempt property and calls bouncer()->allow() only when acl()->getRoles() contains the current route. admin.tinymce.upload is absent from the ACL role map, so the route receives authentication but no route-specific ACL check.
corrected_fields.reasoning: Replace the ACL sentence with: Auth on 2.2.x is supplied by the user middleware around Admin routes; because admin.tinymce.upload has no entry in acl()->getRoles(), Bouncer performs no route-specific permission check after authenticating an eligible staff user.
